newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Police expand search for wanted Sri Lankan MP.
newsitem.headline: Police expand search for wanted Sri Lankan MP.

text.p: One of two key suspects in the killing of a Sri Lankan legislator has turned himself in to a Colombo judge as police expanded the search for the second suspect, a senior police officer said on Monday.

Mahinda Ratnatilleke, the main opposition party's mayoral candidate for the southern city of Ratnapura, surrendered on Sunday at the home of the magistrate for Fort, the central part of Colombo, a senior Ratnapura police officer told Reuters.
Ratnatilleke was remanded until Thursday when he is to be presented before the Ratnapura magistrate, said the officer, a member of the investigating team. He declined to be named.
The other named suspect in the case, legislator Susantha Punchinilame of the main opposition United National Party (UNP), was still at large, he said.
"We expect him to surrender to courts shortly as he can't hide forever," the officer said. "We have intensified the manhunt for him."
Police have questioned more than 800 people and arrested 11 suspects, mostly junior UNP activists, so far, he said.
Last Tuesday's killing of ruling People's Alliance lawmaker Nalanda Ellawala during a roadside quarrel with UNP supporters harked back to an age of political violence in the late 1980s.

The slaying sparked two days of riots last week in the gem mining town of Ratnapura, 80 km (50 miles) southeast of Colombo. Pro-People's Alliance mobs set fire to scores of buildings owned by UNP supporters.
Police had offered a one-million-rupee ($17,500) reward for information leading to the arrest of either Punchinilame or Ratnatilleke.
Ellawala, the youngest member of Sri Lanka's 225-seat parliament and the scion of an influential political family, was cremated last Saturday in a funeral attended by an estimated 100,000 mourners.

Soon after the funeral, about 20 gunmen attacked and robbed a Chinese restaurant owned by a well-known UNP lawmaker in downtown Colombo, but police said it was not clear if this was related to the continuing unrest. No one was hurt.

Ellawala was killed the day before the deadline for filing nominations in the March 21 local government polls, the first UNP-People's Alliance election contest since 1994 when the alliance ended UNP's 17 years in power.
